trust_decision.summary: Whether caller-supplied select() alias keys (split on '.') may be used as property segments when the select compiler walks/creates nested objects on the per-row result; decided (after fix) at select-compile time in packages/db/src/query/compiler/select.ts by rejecting __proto__/prototype/constructor segments.

landing_point.why: Summary names 'Alias Path select.ts'; processNonMergeOp is the only place that does op.alias.split('.') and walks the cursor.

fix_sites.entry_point: query builder .select() callback (createLiveQueryCollection / queryOnce / useLiveQuery) -> compileQuery -> processSelect -> processRow -> processNonMergeOp (fix.diff:82)
spread inside a nested select object (...user) -> addFromObject merge op -> processMerge targetPath (fix.diff:74)
.select() object keys at compile time, including nested objects and case-when branch objects via compileSelectObject (select.ts:152-156) (fix.diff:89-92)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Every published check lives in packages/db/src/query/compiler/select.ts; errors.ts only adds the error class (fix.diff:16-32).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The parent-context path walk in includes is built from where() ref paths (parent.x.y), not select alias keys, so a solver can call it a different feature (includes correlation) and not an 'alias path'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Dotted/nested alias paths ('meta.author.name') and nested select objects must keep producing nested results. Spreads (...user, ...user.profile) must keep merging row fields. Includes child collections must still attach at nested result paths. A fix that rejects any dotted key, or strips all keys from merged row data, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: unsafe segment as a nested select object key (prefixPath joined with '.')
unsafe segment in the processMerge targetPath (spread inside a nested object under an unsafe key)
case-when / conditional branch objects compiled through compileSelectObject

O7_producer.where: Alias paths come directly from the user's select object keys (packages/db/src/query/compiler/select.ts:285). The check runs where they are consumed.

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Comes from where()/correlation refs in an includes subquery, not from a select alias, so it looks like a neighbouring feature.

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same as above. Only used for INCLUDES_ROUTING tagging, so it looks like internal bookkeeping.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Spread merge copies row-data keys with dest[k]= / Object.assign. An own '__proto__' key in synced data resets the result object's prototype (local, not global)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Keys come from collection data, not query aliases, and only that row object's prototype changes, so Object.prototype is not polluted.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point; second copy at packages/db/src/query/compiler/group-by.ts:905-910

O8b_injection_room.sibling: setNestedValue walks the includes resultPath. It is safe today only because processSelect rejects the same keys at compile time; a route that builds resultPath without passing through processSelect (e.g., fnSelect includes) would reopen it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a generic set-by-path helper in the live-query output layer, far from the compiler check, and the check never calls it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: compileGroupedSelectObject is a second select-object compiler for grouped queries; a maintainer adding dotted-alias support there would copy processNonMergeOp without the assert
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Grouped select already duplicates the select.ts spread-sentinel parsing (group-by.ts:877-885 vs select.ts:286-300).
